chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The kohl (eyeliner) applied at night benefits the eye, and it is an adornment by the day.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between using kohl at night versus during the day according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on personal hygiene, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the reliable chain of Zurarah highlights the dual nature of kohl as both a therapeutic agent and a form of permissible adornment. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing physical health with aesthetic beauty, validating the use of natural remedies while encouraging cleanliness as an aspect of faith.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, from Safwan, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The (application of) the Kohl at night benefits the eyes, and it is an adornment by the day’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Applying eye powder to one’s eyes is beneficial to the eyes and it is beautification during the day.’”
